policy_title: Change the definition of hate crime
stated: Reform UK will change the definition of hate crime, asserting that the current CPS and police definition has led to systemic bias and that members of the public should not be investigated based on 'any' perceived hate crime.

source.quote: Change the Definition of Hate Crime The CPS and police definition of a hate crime has led to systemic bias. Members of the British public must not be investigated because ‘any’ person ‘perceives’ that a hate crime has been committed.

bearing_set.reason: Changing hate crime definitions directly reshapes how crimes are recorded, investigated, and prosecuted by police and CPS — a core crime/justice system measure.

Hate crime law is the primary legal-rights framework protecting minorities from discriminatory targeting; redefining it materially alters equal treatment and anti-discrimination protections for those groups, which is squarely within O9's scope.

The policy explicitly objects to the 'any perceived' investigation threshold, targeting state surveillance and coercive investigation of lawful speech/expression — a direct bearing on freedom from state coercion and speech freedoms under O10.

membership_note: This policy creates a genuine O9/O10 tradeoff: what reduces state coercion over speech (improves O10) simultaneously narrows the protective framework for targeted minorities (worsens O9). Both bearings clear the non-negligible bar with concrete mechanisms. O5 is not separately scored — the effect on actual crime rates or justice outcomes is secondary and subsumed by the definitional/enforcement mechanism already captured in O9.
